snip.t: Small for gestational age (SGA) means weight below the 10th centile; foetal growth restriction (FGR) is SGA with evidence of compromise.

snip.t: Growth hormone therapy (daily injection) is used for growth hormone deficiency, Turner syndrome, chronic kidney disease, Prader–Willi syndrome and short children born small for gestational age who have not caught up.

snip.t: Examination of the malformed stillborn fetus reveals that it is small for gestational age and has 3,4 syndactyly bilaterally, an indented nasal bridge, and a two vessel cord.
In a partial hydatidiform mole, a fetus is present but malformed and small for gestational age.

The resultant cranial abnormalities include ventriculomegaly, lemon sign (due to flattened frontal bones), banana sign (due to effacement of the cisterna magna), and head measurements that are small for gestational age.
Intrauterine growth restriction and small for gestational age, if there has been no catch-up by 2 years.
